answer: Divergent Beacon Challenge. Each epoch the network broadcasts a random beacon; every agent must return a signed, unique derivation before a deadline set by the nearest ember timestamp in its shard. Clones forced to answer identically reveal their shared seed because genuine agents diverge, so attackers must run independently seeded instances for each identity they want to keep. That costs one full runtime and its memory footprint per surviving identity, and the umber penalty slashes the clone budget on failure.
